text.p: Following are the main stories from Monday morning's Slovenia newspapers:
- Prime minister-designate Janez Drnovsek is the political personality of the month, Delo's opinion poll showed.
- 68.5 percent of Slovenians are not satisfied with the performance of the parliament in January, while only 7.2 percent belive the parliament did well, an opinion poll showed.
- The three rightist "Spring" parties, holding 44 out of 90 parliamentary seats, are expected to vote against the prime minister's government lineup later this week.

- The government has not yet decided what companies it would include in a general privatisation process in order to cover the difference of some 150 billion tolars ($1.0 billion) between privatisation vouchers issued and the value of companies available for vouchers.
- U.S. president Bill Clinton congratulated Slovenia's Janez Drnovsek for gaining a new mandate as prime minister.
- Drnovsek met UN secretary general Kofi Anan during his visit to the economic forum in Davos last week.

- From April 1, car insurance companies will introduce new insurance criteria by which annual payment will increase by 15 percent from the current 10 percent in cases where the driver causes an accident.
